summary: Research phase complete for cycle 001. Ran a live literature review (16 sources, each read at least at abstract level, several in full), verified the fixture with `study.py check` (train 1078 / validation 359 / test 360), and wrote the three required deliverables. No models were trained and no test data was accessed. Key finding: under the registered constants (lr 1e-3, λ 0.01, 850 steps), AdamW decay shrinks weights by about 0.85% over the run, so the expected effect on accuracy is small and the registered CI is likely to span zero. The study cannot resolve effects much below about 2.5 pp.
evidence: cycles/001/research/sources.json: 16 entries with id, title, url, summary, license, accessed_at; validated as JSON.
cycles/001/research/protocol.json: registered hypothesis, primary metric, bootstrap plan (10000 resamples, seed 2026), and falsification rule, all read and used unchanged.
python study.py check (cycle 001) printed status passed, dataset_shape [1797, 64], split sizes train 1078 / validation 359 / test 360.
Installed torch 2.14.1 .venv torch/optim/adam.py:419 executes param.mul_(1 - lr * weight_decay) when decoupled_weight_decay is True (grep and sed of source).
Arithmetic: 17 steps/epoch x 50 epochs = 850 steps; (1-1e-5)^850 = 0.99154 (about 0.85% shrink); sensitivity arm (1-1e-6)^850 = 0.99915 (about 0.085%).
UCI optdigits page (fetched): CC BY 4.0 license; the 1797 sklearn samples correspond to the UCI test file (training file has 3823 examples); scikit-learn BSD line covers code and docs only.
PyTorch AdamW docs (fetched 2.15 page): defaults lr=0.001, weight_decay=0.01; decoupled decay sentence and paper link.
Nanda explore/understand/distill stage definitions read from the LessWrong mirror of hjMy4ZxS5ogA9cTYK; the sequence index URL in the protocol was verified.
CUDA check: torch.cuda.is_available() True, device NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop GPU (not used for training in this phase).
issues: The percentile-bootstrap method (used by the registered 10000-resample CI) is supported only by an abstract-level source (S15); it must be sourced in full before the analysis phase computes the CI.

Zhang et al. (S07), Loshchilov & Hutter (S01), Krogh & Hertz (S08), Bjorck et al. (S09), Zhou et al. (S10), Lipton & Steinhardt (S11), and Lones (S12) were read at abstract level or from search summaries only; their numeric claims are not verified here.

The shuffled_labels control runs only with weight_decay 0.01 and has no unregularized counterpart, so it cannot isolate the decay effect on memorization. This is a stated limitation; the protocol is immutable.

The registered falsification rule covers only the directional H1 (decay > 0). It does not say what counts as support when the CI is wholly below 0 for a secondary effect; the analysis must follow the written rule.
Seed-to-seed variance is estimated from only three seeds and is not captured by the test-example bootstrap; per-seed effects and SDs must be reported alongside the CI.
A search returned a Nanda post (sYHrW4wwfoMBxNDcA) that is not the protocol's cited sequence; it is not cited.
Licensing: the fixture's data is CC BY 4.0 (UCI), not BSD; attribution is required in the paper.
Safetensors license (S16) and PyTorch repo license were not verified.
objective: Complete the research phase of the registered AdamW weight-decay validation cycle: literature review, source ledger, predictions and alternatives recorded before any training, and highlights/anomalies. The pilot and comparisons are later phases.
predictions: P1: the paired mean accuracy difference (decay 0.01 minus 0) is within ±1.0 pp (about 70% confidence).
P2: the paired 95% bootstrap CI includes 0, which the protocol treats as inconclusive (about 75%).
P3: the CI lies wholly above 0, supporting H1 (about 10–15%).
P4: real-label MLP test accuracy is 0.93–0.99, and the logistic baseline is 0.94–0.98 (about 80%).
P5: the shuffled-label arm reaches near-chance test accuracy (about 0.10); above 0.20 would indicate a leakage or bug (about 90%).
P6: class-prior test accuracy is about the test-split majority fraction (about 0.10).
P7: seed-to-seed SD of test accuracy is 0.3–1.5 pp, comparable to or above any decay effect (about 60%).
P8: regularized and unregularized loss histories differ at float precision; identical histories would mean decay is not applied (about 99%).

Mechanistic: under the registered constants, weights shrink by about 0.85% over the run from decay 0.01, and about 0.085% for the sensitivity arm. This is arithmetic from the code and constants, not measured.
alternatives: No decay effect: at this budget the decay shrink (~0.85%) is much smaller than Adam's update, so predictions barely change.
Regularization reduces accuracy: a strong decay could push the shrink to matter, but at 0.01 it is unlikely, so this is a weak alternative for the registered arms.
Apparent gain from seed or order randomness: controlled by the paired design, but three seeds leave seed variance poorly estimated.
Implementation error: the decay is not applied, shown by identical loss histories (P8), or the labels leak (P5).
Resolution limit: the 360-example test set and about 3% disagreement give a minimum detectable difference near 2.5 pp, so a real effect smaller than that will be reported as inconclusive.
Shuffled-label control confound: without an unregularized shuffled arm, memorization differences cannot be attributed to decay.
observations: The protocol's constants make the intervention very small. The fixture does not log weight norms, so the shrink is an expectation, not an observation.
The protocol's cited Nanda sequence is correct; one search result was a different post and was excluded.
The fixture passed its check command with the expected split sizes, and CUDA is available on an RTX 5070 Laptop GPU.
Prior evidence for decoupled decay comes mostly from large image models; this study uses a small MLP on 1078 training examples, so the transfer is uncertain.
The data license is CC BY 4.0 via UCI, which requires attribution, while the scikit-learn BSD line covers only its code and docs.
learning: Reading the update rule and computing the shrink before training shows that this study is designed to test a near-null intervention at a small budget. The expected outcome is inconclusive, and the main open question is whether the protocol can detect any decay effect, not whether decay helps. The seed-level results and per-seed SD will show this more directly than the pooled CI. The bootstrap resamples test examples only, so it does not measure training variance, and the shuffled-label control is not paired with an undecayed arm.
rationale: The research deliverables are complete and verified: the source ledger parses, the predictions are recorded before training, and the protocol was not edited. The next phase needs the pilot (validation only) to run. The gaps are listed as issues. Nothing blocks the next phase, so the decision is to continue.
